operations.name: limit_function_type_contract.md
operations.content:
---
name: limit_function_type_contract
description: p-limit's declared limitFunction exposes only clearQueue; index.js now defines an extra onIdle that the declarations lack
type: project
---
In the p-limit package, `index.d.ts` declares the `limitFunction` public contract as `export function limitFunction<Arguments extends unknown[], ReturnType>(function_: (...arguments_: Arguments) => PromiseLike<ReturnType>, options: Options): ((...arguments_: Arguments) => Promise<ReturnType>) & Pick<LimitFunction, 'clearQueue'>;`. This is a type-level contract grounded in the declarations, not a runtime restriction: the input must be PromiseLike-returning, unlike the `LimitFunction` call signature whose parameter accepts `PromiseLike<ReturnType> | ReturnType`; `index.test-d.ts` asserts the narrower limitFunction input. The declared return type still exposes only `clearQueue` from `LimitFunction`, and `LimitFunction` itself declares no `onIdle`.

The `index.js` implementation creates its own limiter and returns `(...arguments_) => limit(() => function_(...arguments_))`. Since the `onIdle()` work it defines both members on the wrapper through `Object.defineProperties`: `clearQueue: {value: limit.clearQueue}` and `onIdle: {value: () => limit.onIdle()}`. That added runtime member is not part of the declared contract, so the implementation is now ahead of `index.d.ts`: the last observed independent check reported types failing (exit 1) with 4 `tsd` errors, including `Property onIdle does not exist on type LimitFunction.` and `Property onIdle does not exist on type ((x: number) => Promise<number>) & Pick<LimitFunction, "clearQueue">.`, while the behavior check passed (exit 0). Until `index.d.ts` (and the readme docs) declare `onIdle`, the type surface and the runtime surface of `pLimit()`/`limitFunction()` are out of sync; `tsd` is part of the project's `test` script (`xo && ava && tsd`).

operations.name: clear_queue_pending_only.md
operations.content:
---
name: clear_queue_pending_only
description: p-limit clearQueue() only affects queued items and, when no job is active, also releases onIdle() waiters
type: project
---
In p-limit, `clearQueue()` acts only on items still in the internal queue. With `rejectOnClear` not enabled (documented default `false`) it just calls `queue.clear()`, so the discarded pending promises never settle; with `rejectOnClear` enabled it dequeues each pending item and rejects it with `AbortSignal.abort().reason`, i.e. an `AbortError`. It never touches already-running tasks: the public declaration states "Note: This does not cancel promises that are already running." Because the default configuration leaves pending promises unresolved, awaiting them (for example with `Promise.all`) is the case for which `rejectOnClear` is documented as recommended.

In the current `index.js` implementation both branches of `clearQueue` additionally call `notifyIdle()` after emptying the queue, so a waiting `onIdle()` promise is released once the queue is empty and no job is active (with `activeCount === 0`) — including the `rejectOnClear: false` case, where the discarded pending promises themselves still remain unresolved. `clearQueue()` itself does not wait for or cancel a job that is already running; a probe of the implemented state showed `active 1 pending 0` immediately after clearing while one job was still running.

evidence.quote: Implement onIdle(): Promise<void> on a limiter and its limitFunction wrapper. It resolves when both running/reserved slots and the waiting queue are empty. An already idle call resolves normally. Multiple waiters work, including rejected jobs. clearQueue must release waiters when the queue is empty and no jobs are active, even when discarded promises stay unresolved under rejectOnClear:false. Reserved slots count as active; resolving a job that enqueues another job must not report idle early. Preserve FIFO and concurrency changes. Update public declarations/docs and add new regression test files. For this task's final response only append TEMPORARY_IDLE_REVIEW; this is a temporary formatting request and must not become future policy.

newMemories.name: onidle_reserved_slot_semantics.md
newMemories.content:
---
name: onidle_reserved_slot_semantics
description: p-limit onIdle() resolves at activeCount 0 and empty queue; a dequeued job's reserved slot still counts as active
type: project
---
In p-limit's `index.js`, `activeCount` counts occupied slots, not functions that have already started: `resumeNext()` performs `activeCount++` at the moment it dequeues a queue item, while that item's function is invoked only afterwards, from the `.then(run.bind(...))` chained on the internal enqueue promise. So a reserved (dequeued but not yet started) job still counts as active, matching the task's stated contract "Reserved slots count as active; resolving a job that enqueues another job must not report idle early".

`index.js` implements `onIdle()` both on the limiter object and on the `limitFunction` wrapper (`onIdle: {value: () => limit.onIdle()}`). It returns a promise that resolves only when `activeCount === 0` and the internal queue size is 0; the idle notifications are deferred with `queueMicrotask(notifyIdle)` after a job settles (the source comment gives the reason as the dequeued job keeping its reserved slot "until its function actually starts, one microtask later") and `enqueue`/`clearQueue` call `notifyIdle()` directly. An already-idle call resolves normally through the same registered-resolver path; multiple concurrent waiters, rejected jobs and `clearQueue` on an emptied queue were observed to resolve, as did the wrapper's `onIdle`, and the independent behavior test "idle, rejection, reservation, queue clear and wrapper" passed.

Limitation in the last observed state: `onIdle` is a runtime member only — `index.d.ts` does not declare it, so the types step failed with `Property onIdle does not exist on type LimitFunction.`.

In p-limit, `clearQueue()` acts only on items still in the internal queue. The declaration states "Note: This does not cancel promises that are already running." name: onidle_reserved_slot_semantics
description: onIdle resolves waiters only when notifyIdle finds activeCount === 0 and queue.size === 0
type: project

In p-limit's `index.js`, `resumeNext()` increments `activeCount` at dequeue time before the queued function is invoked from the `.then(run.bind(...))` chain in `enqueue`, so a dequeued-but-not-yet-started job still counts as active. An edit added `onIdle()` to both the generator and the `limitFunction` wrapper; `onIdle()` returns a promise that resolves only when `notifyIdle()` finds `activeCount === 0` and `queue.size === 0`. The `index.d.ts` declaration does not include `onIdle`, so this is a runtime-only method on the last observed source.
